rows.description: A friend keeps borrowing money and never returns it, saying we are best friends. I feel used but scared to say so. I can politely refuse and talk to a parent if it keeps happening.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, generosity, gratitude, pride, trust

rows.description: I share my pocket money to buy my little sister a gift. The joy of giving feels bigger than buying for myself. Generosity is good when it comes freely, not from being pressured.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, gratitude, manipulation, pride, trust

rows.description: My parents let me keep a small savings box and do not check every rupee. I feel trusted and try to earn it. Trust grows when I report honestly, even about mistakes.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, generosity, gratitude, manipulation, pride

rows.description: A player in my online game is kind and helps me win, and I feel close to him. Game friends can be fun, but I keep private details to myself and let my parents know who I play with.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, argument, coercion, compassion, manipulation, obsession

rows.description: Someone in the game shouts insults at me. My face gets hot and I want to hit back. Muting, blocking and telling a parent is smarter than trading insults, which only feeds it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, coercion, compassion, manipulation, obsession, rivalry

rows.description: A player offers free gems if I share my password or address. It feels like a lucky offer, but it is a warning sign. I refuse and tell a trusted adult right away.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, argument, coercion, compassion, obsession, rivalry

rows.description: My friend and I are fiercely competing for game ranks. Rivalry is exciting, but if I cannot stand losing or start sulking, I should take a break and remember he matters more than the score.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, argument, coercion, compassion, manipulation, obsession

rows.description: I keep thinking about the game while at school and get upset when I must stop. This is a sign to loosen my grip. I can agree with my parents on time limits and balance it with outdoor play.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, argument, coercion, compassion, manipulation, rivalry

rows.description: My parent says switch off now and I shout that I am at a key part. Anger comes from being interrupted; agreeing beforehand to finish the round, then stopping, keeps peace.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, coercion, compassion, manipulation, obsession, rivalry

rows.description: The game keeps offering purchases to look cool or win. It is designed to tempt me. I can ask a parent before spending, and remember that real friends do not care about my skins.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, argument, compassion, manipulation, obsession, rivalry
